messages:
maya: Quick summary — finished the apples-to-apples load run comparing JSON-mode + function-calls vs plain text streaming under two traffic profiles (synthetic poisson, replay harness). Raw notes below, flagging a regression we should triage.

maya: TL;DR: JSON-mode adds ~6-12% CPU and 7-15% p95 latency depending on KV cache hit rate; function-call validation failures cause retries that blow up tail.

dmitri: Nice. Which model config and kernel path?

maya: Using `rwd-xl-quant` with autokernel selection enabled. Two kernel families exercised: optimized attention (kernel-v3) and fallback slow path (kernel-compat). Kernel switch threshold triggered when sequence len distribution hit >1% >2k tokens in batch (we hit that in synthetic burst).

sara: Can you paste the harness config?

maya: Sure — synthetic and replay harness snippets:
```
# synthetic profile (poisson): rate=120rps, concurrency=64, seq_mean=350, tail=2200(0.8%)
# replay harness: sample from prod-24h (anon), preserved inter-arrival, pinned agent headers
loadgen: --clients=48 --think=poisson --replay-file=sample24h.json
validation: json_mode=true, validate_schema=true, retries_on_validation=true, max_retries=2
```

alex: were KV cache hits varied? that affects latency a lot.

maya: Yes. We ran three KV profiles: cold (0% hits), warm (60% hits), hot (96% hits). Results below are p50/p95 generation-only (ms) and end-to-end with JSON validation (ms).

maya: Cold: gen p50=82 p95=410 | end2end p50=95 p95=467

maya: Warm: gen p50=70 p95=220 | end2end p50=78 p95=250

maya: Hot: gen p50=62 p95=120 | end2end p50=66 p95=132

dmitri: So as expected validation overhead is ~10-15% on tail when KV is cold. But you mentioned a regression?

maya: Right — in synthetic burst run we saw kernel fallback thrash. Kernel-v3 compiled kernels have ~8-10% lower latency; when the autokernel selector flipped mid-run (small fraction of batches), p95 spiked by extra ~9% beyond the JSON overhead. The selector logs show oscillation because the replay harness had mixed seq lengths.

sara: Any evidence of validation-triggered retries inflating load?

maya: Yes — ~0.6% of calls hit validation failure because the model produced trailing commas in `results.items` for JSON-mode. Retries were synchronous, so each retry re-entered the queue (no cached prompt), doubling tail for those requests. On warm profile that bumped error-class p99 from 1.2s to 2.6s for affected requests.

alex: Ugh. Do we have a minimal repro prompt?

maya: Pasted example that caused trailing comma: "items": [ {"id":1, "name":"a"}, ] — the model occasionally emits the extra comma on tool-call outputs when temperature=0.1 and top_k unset.

dmitri: Good catch. For mitigation ideas: 1) add permissive JSON parser that strips trailing commas before marking as validation failure (fast path). 2) make retries async/backoff (don't requeue at head). 3) tighten autokernel hysteresis to avoid flapping.

sara: Agree. Also we should measure CPU overhead of permissive parsing vs current strict validation. Could be cheaper than a full retry.

maya: I ran a quick microbench: Rust permissive parse (strip+parse) ~0.35ms/op vs strict serde ~0.52ms/op on p99 small payloads. So it's cheaper and probably worth adding.

perf-bot: ci:loadtest #1768345601 finished — summary: synthetic-run: errors=0.9% (validation_retries=0.6%), avg_cpu=74%, p95_overall=478ms (+12% vs baseline), kernel_fallback_rate=3.1%

alex: Based on that we should: A) implement permissive pre-parse + metrics tag, B) change retry behavior to schedule delayed retry (jitter), C) add a kernel-selector smoothing window (500ms) to avoid flip-flops. Agree?

dmitri: +1. For (C) we need to be careful not to delay real beneficial switches for long sequences. Maybe use request-level hinting: if a batch contains >=5% sequences >1k, prefer stability window instead of immediate hot-swapping.

sara: I'll slot a perf spike P0 with those 3 changes. Can someone open a PR for permissive parse?

maya: I'll do the permissive parse PR and include microbench harness + feature flag `json.permissive=true`. I'll also attach the replay/strict comparison artifacts to the PR.

alex: I'll take retry/backoff changes. Dmitri can you own kernel-selector smoothing?

dmitri: On it. Will prototype smoothing + config knobs.

perf-bot: note: pushed artifact links -> https://artifacts.internal/loadtests/1768345601/ (contains raw traces, flamegraphs, kernel-switch logs)

maya: Thanks everyone. I'll open the thread PR and link here when ready :thumbsup:

ci-bot: deploy-checklist: permissive-parse feature flag set to off by default; warn on canary if validation_failures drop >0.1%

alex: Cool. Follow-up: let's add a replay harness case that forces high variance sequence lengths to ensure no selector oscillation.

maya: Added as test-case `mixed_seq_lengths_highvar.json` in the artifacts. End of notes.
